description: TASK DDL and execution asserted through the SQL surface - SHOW TASKS cells (state is spelled lower-case started/suspended; the schedule text distinguishes an interval from a CRON expression; definition carries the body) and each task body's side effects. Covers CREATE with an interval and with USING CRON, ALTER TASK RESUME / SUSPEND, DROP, EXECUTE TASK running the body once, a task created over a stream neither consuming the stream nor starting itself, and a CALL-bodied task executing its procedure. Converted 1:1 from features/TasksTest (now retired). The two execution-result tests keep the class's live exemption as skip snowflake: live EXECUTE TASK is asynchronous, so a shared session cannot await the body's side effects.

CREATE TASK daily_cleanup
WAREHOUSE = 'COMPUTE_WH'
SCHEDULE = '60 MINUTES'
AS DELETE FROM logs WHERE timestamp < '2024-01-01'

CREATE TASK hourly_job
WAREHOUSE = 'COMPUTE_WH'
SCHEDULE = 'USING CRON 0 * * * * UTC'
AS INSERT INTO summary SELECT * FROM staging
SELECT STARTSWITH("schedule", 'USING CRON') FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID())) WHERE "name" = 'HOURLY_JOB'

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE refresh_data() RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS
BEGIN INSERT INTO ran_marker VALUES ('ran'); RETURN 'ok'; END

CREATE OR REPLACE TASK refresh_task
